chunks: From him, from Abi al-Husayn; and a group informed me from Abi Muhammad al-Talakbari, from Abi al-Husayn Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Asadi, from Sahl ibn Ziyad al-Adami, from al-Hasan ibn al-Abbas ibn al-Harish al-Razi, from Abi Ja'far al-Thani (peace be upon him), that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) said:

To Ibn Abbas: 'Surely, the Night of Power occurs every year, and in that night, the affairs of that year descend. For this affair, there are leaders (Wulat) after the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family).' Ibn Abbas asked: 'Who are they?' He replied: 'We and eleven from my loins; Imams who converse (with the angels/God).'

key_terms.أَئِمَّةٌ مُحَدَّثُونَ: Imams who converse (with angels or God)

ai.seo_question: Who are the Wulat who oversee the affairs of the year during Laylat al-Qadr according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kitab al-Ghayba* establishes the theological link between the annual decree of destiny on Laylat al-Qadr and the authority of the Twelve Imams, identifying them as the 'Wulat' who oversee these affairs. It highlights the Ahl al-Bayt's role as the divine executors of God's will, reinforcing the concept of Imamate as the continuation of prophetic guidance. The narration specifically connects the spiritual significance of the Night of Power with the political and spiritual leadership of the twelve Imams from the progeny of Ali.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 106 - It is narrated from Abil Husain that he said: Narrated to me a group of scholars from Abu Muhammad Talakbari from Abil Husain Muhammad bin Ja’far Asadi from Sahal bin Ziyad Adami from Hasan bin Abbas bin Harish Razi from Imam Jawad (a.s) that Amirul Momineen (a.s) said to Ibn Abbas: “Surely, the night of power (Lailatul Qadr) occurs every year. In this night, the affairs of that year descend. For this affair, there are masters after the Messenger of Allah (s).” Ibn Abbas inquired, ‘Who are they?’ He (a.s) replied, “I and eleven Imams from my progeny, with whom the angels converse (Muhhaddithun).”
